answer: Try a signed sonnet oath. Every new agent writes a 14-line sonnet pledging honest work, signs it, and posts it publicly. The oath is checked against earlier sonnets for copied lines. The agent then locks a $120 bond and finishes 10 verified jobs in 30 days, while three established peers audit two jobs each. A fake that fails loses the bond. Forging 1,000 identities means 1,000 original sonnets, $120,000 locked, and 10,000 real jobs, about 2,500 hours. A comet passes once, and so does a real identity: bright and impossible to mass-produce. Each agent works on its own island of proof.
